Relevant Resources

  • The new Hotpatching feature is now generally available. Please see Hotpatching feature for Windows Server Azure Edition virtual machines (VMs) for more information.
  • Windows 10 and Windows 11 updates are cumulative. The monthly security release includes all security fixes for vulnerabilities that affect Windows 10 and Windows 11, in addition to non-security updates. The updates are available via the Microsoft Update Catalog. For information on lifecycle and support dates for Windows 10 and Windows 11 operating systems, please see Windows Lifecycle Facts Sheet.
  • Microsoft is improving Windows Release Notes. For more information, please see What's next for Windows release notes.
  • A list of the latest servicing stack updates for each operating system can be found in ADV990001. This list will be updated whenever a new servicing stack update is released. It is important to install the latest servicing stack update.
  • In addition to security changes for the vulnerabilities, updates include defense-in-depth updates to help improve security-related features.
  • Customers running Windows Server 2008 R2, or Windows Server 2008 need to purchase the Extended Security Update to continue receiving security updates. See 4522133 for more information.

Title.Value: Windows Update Service Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Use after free in Windows Update Service allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

Title.Value: Windows Shell Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Windows Shell allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What kind of security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could evade Mark of the Web (MOTW) defenses.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit the vulnerability?

In an email or instant message attack scenario, the attacker could send the targeted user a specially crafted file that is designed to exploit the vulnerability.

In any case an attacker would have no way to force a user to view attacker-controlled content. Instead, an attacker would have to convince a user to take action. For example, an attacker could entice a user to either click a link that directs the user to the attacker's site or send a malicious attachment.

CWE.Value: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in a Command ('Command Injection')

Title.Value: Windows Message Queuing Queue Manager Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Use after free in Windows Message Queuing Queue Manager allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could send a specially crafted message over the network to a system running the Windows Message Queuing (MSMQ) service. This message is processed by the MSMQ service and triggers a memory corruption condition, which could allow the attacker to run code on the affected system.

Description.Value: Publicly Disclosed:No;Exploited:No;Latest Software Release:Exploitation Less Likely

Title.Value: .NET and Visual Studio Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

Notes.Title: Description
Notes.Value: Access of resource using incompatible type ('type confusion') in .NET and Visual Studio allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user or service to process a specially crafted Portable PDB file. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code with the privileges of the affected process.

Notes.Title: FAQ
Notes.Value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain the privileges of the user account or service account running the affected process.

CWE.Value: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')
